prerequisites: Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline

learning_outcomes.text: Students recognize the field of forming technology as a complex system of material science, plasto-mechanical, process- and information-technical elements.

They possess detailed, comprehensive knowledge of the material science and plasticity theory fundamentals, the process technology of sheet, hot, and cold bulk forming, as well as the latest tool technology with its specific material and manufacturing problems.
They master computational and experimental investigation methods to describe the accuracy behavior of forming machines under load and to design automation.

Students apply computer-aided analysis methods based on product CAD data to define the overall forming process in the preparatory, forming, and post-processing steps. Special emphasis must be placed on the design of the operation sequence.

Students are able to use state-of-the-art CAE software tools to handle the central tasks of forming companies - methods planning, tool design, and the integration of forming processes into productive value chains. They plan product and process optimizations considering the entire product development chain. They can present and defend the results in meetings.

syllabus_topics: Foundations and connections: manufacturing processes, manufacturing technologies, efficiency, sustainability
Process-specific requirements for machines and tools, equipment for single-part production
Mechanical presses, hydraulic forming machines, characteristic values of machine tools, constructive design, execution variants, fields of application
Forming: mechanisms of plastic deformation, flow curves and formability, plasticity theory, friction, machine and tool technology, process chains, hot forming vs. cold forming
Manufacturing techniques in industrial process chains: linking production and manufacturing processes, coordination and control of processes, technical availability, economic considerations
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is determined by the lecturers: either a written examination or an oral examination. The duration and scope of the graded examination are according to the applicable study regulations (Klausur) or general examination regulations (mündliche Prüfung). For the unassessed experimental work, 3 to 5 experimental tasks are processed.
